subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: Should stale background PTY exec trees from a previous gateway epoch be killed on startup, or should OpenClaw persist enough metadata to re-register them?
rationale: Both options affect long-running user work, resource cleanup, and session-state semantics, and the open linked PR intentionally avoids that cold-start policy decision.

options.title: Kill stale PTY trees
options.body: Treat previous-epoch PTY exec trees as unsafe orphans and terminate them during startup reconciliation with clear logging.

options.title: Re-register live runs
options.body: Persist enough metadata to restore visibility for still-live PTY runs and only kill entries that cannot be safely reattached.

options.title: Land only in-process drift repair
options.body: Accept the linked PR's narrower in-process reconciliation and keep durable restart cleanup as a separate design item.

recommendation.title: Kill stale PTY trees
recommendation.body: Treat previous-epoch PTY exec trees as unsafe orphans and terminate them during startup reconciliation with clear logging.

likelyOwner.reason: The background exec session registry and timeout behavior history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the restart policy choice.
